title: Runtime and CLI Reference
text: Runtime and CLI Reference How AIWAF works: system architecture AIWAF exposes language-specific middleware, engine, and CLI APIs. There is no shared /api/v1 bearer-token management service in the current repo. Python # Unified CLI aiwaf --help aiwaf blacklist migrate aiwaf status # Django management commands python manage.py detect_and_train python manage.py regenerate_model python manage.py aiwaf_reset --keywords --confirm python manage.py aiwaf_logging --status python manage.py geo_block_country list # Explicit adapter dispatch aiwaf django aiwaf_list --all aiwaf flask --help aiwaf fast --help Node.js cd js AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG=/path/to/access.log npm run train npm run aiwaf -- status npm run aiwaf -- list blacklist npm run aiwaf -- add blacklist 203.0.113.9 "manual block" npm run aiwaf -- add ip-exemption 203.0.113.10 "trusted monitor" npm run aiwaf -- geo summary npm run aiwaf -- model info npm run aiwaf -- export aiwaf-export.json Use Redis or another shared cache for consistent rate limiting across multiple Node processes. Without shared state, the in-memory fallback is process-local. In an application with the npm package installed, use npx aiwaf --help ; the source commands above run from js/ . Java aiwaf-cli status aiwaf-cli diagnose --model model.json aiwaf-cli blocked aiwaf-cli unblock 203.0.113.10 aiwaf-cli train --events events.json --out model.json --backend java aiwaf-cli model status --path model.json Adapter and binding references Python adapters Node.js entry points Java engine Rust/Python and WASM functions Website endpoints This Flask documentation application defines its own /health , /aiwaf/status , /aiwaf/whitelist , /aiwaf/blacklist , and /aiwaf/keywords routes. Those are website-specific handlers, not a portable AIWAF API. Their implementation does not provide the bearer-token authentication previously described here.

title: How AIWAF Works
text: How AIWAF Works AIWAF sits inside the application request lifecycle. Framework adapters turn live HTTP requests into policy inputs, deterministic controls make immediate decisions, and optional anomaly models add evidence from recent behavior. On this page Two connected execution paths Responsibilities of each layer How route policies become decisions A block is a decision; a blocklist is state State ownership explains multi-worker behavior How anomaly detection contributes The learning loop What happens after the handler Read the runtime internals Two connected execution paths The system has a request path for enforcing the current policy and a learning path for improving future decisions. Configuration, route metadata, runtime stores, and model artifacts connect them. Framework adapter Extract method, path, headers, client address, and available handler metadata. Policy and checks Select applicable protections, read state, and return an early denial when a check fails. Application handler Allowed requests reach the normal application code. Response observations Record status, duration, and behavior; response-aware adapters may make another decision. This is a conceptual flow, not a universal middleware ordering. Python wrappers, Node middleware, and Java filters attach to different framework hooks. The runtime-specific pages below explain the actual execution boundaries. Responsibilities of each layer Layer Responsibility Example Adapter Read framework request/response data and intercept execution. Django middleware, Express middleware, Spring filter. Policy planner Combine enabled middleware with route metadata and path rules. A webhook may run header checks without form timing. Deterministic checks Enforce concrete limits and matching rules. A rate window over its configured maximum returns a denial. Behavior model Score a feature vector using a trained forest. Repeated unknown-route probes can add anomaly evidence. Runtime state Remember recent activity, exemptions, blocks, and learned keywords. A later request observes an active IP block. Learning pipeline Build future models and keyword state from recorded traffic. A scheduled job trains from access logs. How route policies become decisions A manifest records discovered routes, methods, and inferred handler intent. Source analysis can supply signals such as JSON responses, form handling, or authentication calls when framework metadata is incomplete. The manifest compiler translates those signals into middleware disablement and rate-limit overrides. The runtime combines those generated rules with explicitly configured path policies and decorator or annotation metadata. A protection runs only when it is enabled and applicable under that runtime's policy rules. An auto selection starts from the canonical set and omits checks unsupported by detected application signals; it is not itself an anomaly detector. For example, an API endpoint may omit HTML form timing while keeping headers and rate limits. A login form needs different checks. Keep inferred policies reviewable: a route name or return type is evidence about intent, not proof of authorization. A block is a decision; a blocklist is state A failing header, method, or rate check can reject the current request. Some checks also record an offense or create a temporary IP block. Those are separate effects: returning a denial does not imply that every later request is permanently blocked. Reputation handling records weighted offenses and can escalate temporary block durations. Later requests consult block expiry and exemption rules. Which checks mutate reputation and which response statuses they return are runtime-specific. State ownership explains multi-worker behavior State category Typical contents Architectural consequence Recent enforcement state Rate buckets, form timestamps, UUID scores, recent request history. Independent worker memory creates independent windows and counts. Operational stores Blacklists, exemptions, geo policy, learned keywords. Persistence across restarts is different from consistent access across processes. Model artifacts Forest state, feature schema, training metadata. Loading the same artifact does not share rate-limit or blacklist state. A local file can persist data while leaving other request counters process-local. Choose sharing separately for every state category. Java's Redis backend shares enforcement state atomically; Node rate limiting accepts a shared cache; Python sharing depends on the adapter and its configured stores. How anomaly detection contributes An Isolation Forest repeatedly partitions feature samples using random feature choices and split points. Samples isolated in fewer splits tend to receive more anomalous scores. The forest learns a distribution of request behavior; it does not identify a vulnerability or understand the application's authorization rules. The host runtime decides whether a score is enough to block. Model availability, training volume, thresholds, route eligibility, and recent-behavior confirmation can all affect that decision. For example, Node's unknown-route path requires both a sufficiently trained model and scanning-related behavior before issuing an anomaly block. Feature What it describes Why it helps path_len Length of the request path. Unusually long probing paths. kw_hits Matches against malicious keywords. Known probing patterns within a path. resp_time Response duration in seconds. Behavior that differs from the normal timing distribution. status_idx An encoded response-status category. Response outcomes without treating status codes as continuous measurements. burst_count Requests associated with the client in the burst window. Rapid repeated activity. total_404 Not-found responses in the relevant per-client history. Repeated discovery of nonexistent routes. The feature order is part of the model contract. A trainer and scorer must agree on the order, status mapping, time units, and window semantics. Summary fields ending in _ms use milliseconds; the feature vector uses seconds. Sharing feature names alone does not make every model artifact interchangeable. The learning loop Request logs Completed responses supply paths, client identity, status, and timing. Feature extraction Records are normalized and combined with per-client activity windows. Train and review Volume thresholds gate model training; route exemptions filter learned keywords. Publish artifacts The runtime loads persisted model state and updated learned keywords. The training job is separate from ordinary application request handling. Reading logs and rebuilding a forest does not need to happen for every request. Runtime keyword learning, where enabled, is a separate mechanism that can use completed-response signals. Current Python model persistence uses JSON rather than executable Python-object serialization. Java can exchange the Python Rust-model forest state for the supported schema. JavaScript-native artifacts and legacy formats require their own compatibility checks. What happens after the handler Response observations make real status and duration available. This matters for distinguishing a normal request from repeated 404 probing. A response-aware integration may evaluate behavior after the handler returns, but a response already committed or streamed to the client cannot be replaced. Java's Spring filter explicitly distinguishes an uncommitted synchronous response from committed or asynchronous output. Other adapters use their framework's hooks for logging and learning. Avoid assuming that post-response scoring can prevent every byte from leaving the application. Read the runtime internals Python: shared core, framework hooks, policy and training Node.js: middleware order, denial paths and finish hooks Java: engine decisions, Spring discovery and distributed state Rust/WASM: host bindings, matchers and forest implementation

text: Configuration Reference Configuration is adapter-specific. Use the names accepted by your runtime, and apply settings before registering protection. The tables below describe source defaults; they do not guarantee that a middleware is selected or that a route is protected. A shell variable does not automatically become Flask app.config. The middleware reads adapter settings and its own defaults. Django does not automatically read arbitrary environment variables; map them in settings.py. If a config object is supplied, it is used directly rather than rebuilding from config_file/overrides. Custom configuration beans replace auto-configuration where supported. Rust/WASM Arguments to primitive bindings These bindings are not a framework configuration loader. Host adapters control middleware, policy, storage, and proxy handling. Flask and Django flat settings The nested Python table below is the shared configuration manager, primarily exposed through FastAPI. It is not the Flask/Django constructor signature. Their important flat names include AIWAF_RATE_WINDOW (seconds), AIWAF_RATE_MAX and AIWAF_RATE_FLOOD (integer counts), AIWAF_EXEMPT_PATHS (path list), AIWAF_PATH_RULES (rule list), AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_COUNTRIES and AIWAF_GEO_ALLOW_COUNTRIES (country-code lists), and AIWAF_MODEL_PATH (path). Consult each adapter's settings guide for the full flat surface. # Flask: set values before middleware registration. app.config.update( AIWAF_RATE_WINDOW=10, AIWAF_RATE_MAX=20, AIWAF_RATE_FLOOD=40, AIWAF_RATE_CACHE_BACKEND='redis', AIWAF_REDIS_URL='redis://localhost:6379/0', AIWAF_RATE_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX='my-service:rate:', ) AIWAF(app, middlewares=['all']) Flask's rate middleware defaults to 10 seconds, 20 requests, and flood threshold 40. The website overrides these values in app.py. Node's normalized defaults are 60 seconds, 100 requests, and flood threshold 200. Do not use website thresholds as universal package defaults. FastAPI nested options from fastapi import FastAPI from aiwaf.fast import AIWAF app = FastAPI() AIWAF(app, middlewares=['all'], rate_limiting={'window_seconds': 10, 'max_requests': 20, 'flood_threshold': 40, 'cache_backend': 'redis', 'redis_url': 'redis://localhost:6379/0', 'cache_key_prefix': 'my-service:rate:'}) The shared environment loader recognizes names such as AIWAF_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS and AIWAF_RATE_MAX_REQUESTS . Those differ from the Flask/Django flat names. Boolean strings accept true , 1 , yes , and on as true; list mappings split comma-separated values. File lists use JSON arrays. Review the environment map before assuming a setting is supported. Middleware, route policy, and exemptions all selects the canonical middleware set. auto omits checks based on detected application signals. Explicitly disabled middleware and route exemptions can bypass checks even when their configuration says enabled. Regenerate route manifests after route changes and inspect the selected middleware at runtime. Default exemptions differ. Django includes administrative/login paths; Flask includes health, crawler, static and asset paths. Private-address behavior also differs from an explicit trusted-client whitelist. Review Python default exemption lists and the policy lifecycle before interpreting a successful local request as a public-client test. Configure forwarding-header handling with the actual deployment topology. Java exposes trustedProxyCidrs and maxForwardedForEntries . Python and Node extraction use adapter-specific rules; these Java options are not portable knobs. Have the outer proxy overwrite untrusted client forwarding headers, and compare observed client addresses with the intended public client. Multiple workers and storage Persistent blacklist files, model storage, logs, and rate counters have separate ownership. A CSV blacklist does not share every in-memory counter. Flask/FastAPI use separate rate-cache settings; install the Redis client required by the selected backend. Flask can fall back to a process-local cache if Redis initialization fails. Verify repeated requests across workers and inspect backend diagnostics. Node accepts a shared cache implementation; its fallback is process-local. Java Redis shares enforcement state within storageKeyPrefix , supports standalone mode, and defaults to fail_closed . Use the same namespace only for intentionally shared policy/state, and review schema compatibility before mixed-version deployments. Source default tables The Python table includes every leaf returned by the shared manager. The Node table includes normalized options, not every raw option consumed by individual modules (for example cache/WASM settings). The Java table includes public AiwafConfig field initializers. title: Frequently Asked Questions
text: Frequently Asked Questions How AIWAF works: system architecture Where is the source code? Python, Node.js, Rust/WASM, and Java are in the AIWAF monorepo . The root README is authoritative, and each package has its own version and release tag. Can businesses use AIWAF? Yes. The development checkout and future releases expressly distributed under Elastic License 2.0 permit commercial use, modification, redistribution, and consulting, subject to the license conditions. Providing substantial AIWAF functionality to others as a hosted or managed service requires separate permission. ELv2 also prohibits bypassing license-key functionality and removing required notices. Python and Node.js AIWAF will use ELv2 from version 1.1.2 onward . Other packages have independent version numbers. Previously distributed MIT copies retain their MIT permissions. Check the LICENSE and NOTICE in your installed release: retained MIT contributions, dependencies, and the IPinfo Lite database keep their separate terms. The database is provided by IPinfo under CC BY-SA 4.0 . ELv2-covered code is source available. What do I install for Node.js? Use npm install aiwaf and require('aiwaf') . See the Node.js setup guide . Is PHP included? The current monorepo has no PHP implementation or PHP release workflow. Existing PHP pages are retained as legacy reference and are not current setup guidance. Is Rust required for Python? No. Install aiwaf[rust] for native acceleration. Installed capabilities are selected automatically, with Python fallback when unavailable. Version 1.0.8 requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.1 for this extra. Can I reuse old pickle or joblib models? Current Python model persistence uses JSON. Regenerate executable object artifacts through the current trainer. Java supports Python Rust-model JSON state and restricted legacy signed Java artifacts. JavaScript model implementations remain language-native; do not assume every runtime can exchange models. Does an in-memory backend share protection across workers? In-memory state is process-local. Review request logs, trusted-proxy handling, header requirements, rate limits, and path policies. Use narrowly scoped route exemptions and representative staging requests. title: Java Architecture and Response-Aware Enforcement
text: Java Architecture and Response-Aware Enforcement The native Java engine consumes an AiwafRequest and returns an AiwafDecision. Spring and Servlet integrations map HTTP traffic into that contract; storage contexts and model providers are owned by the engine. On this page The engine contracts Two-stage Spring execution Inside the pre-response engine Discovery and configuration before requests arrive Per-engine state and atomic Redis operations Redis failure and upgrade boundaries Response-derived UUID and anomaly evidence Worked example: a missing UUID resource Trace the implementation How AIWAF works: system architecture The engine contracts Contract Purpose AiwafRequest Normalized method, path, client, country, headers, parameters, timing context, and disabled middleware metadata. AiwafConfig Typed limits, exemptions, path rules, storage, model, and observability settings. AiwafDecision Allow or deny outcome with a response status and reason. AiwafEngine Orchestrates checks using its storage context, model provider, UUID lookup, and telemetry. The engine is independent of a controller or servlet response object. Adapters decide how to map an engine decision into HTTP behavior. Java runs natively and does not load the Rust extension. Two-stage Spring execution Map and inspect Discover route metadata, buffer permitted request data, and construct AiwafRequest. Before response evaluateBeforeResponse runs deterministic controls and can prevent controller execution. Controller The allowed request traverses the normal filter chain. After response Use actual status and duration for UUID behavior and anomaly evaluation when the response is still replaceable. AiwafFilter sends an early error for a pre-response denial. After a synchronous handler, it checks whether the response is committed. An uncommitted response can be reset and replaced if the final decision denies it. A committed response is recorded through recordCommittedResponse . Asynchronous completion uses a listener and records once. These paths update relevant history and logs without trying to replace output that has already been sent. The request-only evaluate(request) API remains available and uses provisional status and timing for its AI features. The generic Servlet filter uses that request-time path; Spring's filter has the richer response-aware boundary. Inside the pre-response engine Validate request shape, compressed-body policy, and prohibited Java-serialization payloads. Resolve the path rule, rate overrides, and path/IP exemption state. Reject active blacklisted clients unless the client exemption applies. Enforce the configured method policy. Run applicable keyword, UUID, honeypot, header, geo, and rate/flood checks. Return an allow decision, deferring anomaly scoring for the two-stage API. Each failing stage finalizes a decision and returns early. Path exemptions do not bypass the initial request-shape and method gates, and an exempt path does not automatically bypass an active client blacklist. Geo-only exemptions disable geo enforcement without implying a complete bypass. Discovery and configuration before requests arrive Spring Boot servlet auto-configuration creates the configuration, engine, and ordered filter unless the application supplies replacements. The live MVC mappings expose registered routes and handler annotations. This lets the filter honor route metadata without maintaining a separate controller list. Manifest generation writes discovered routes and policy metadata; PathManifestCore loads and compiles it for the engine. Generated rules are appended after explicit path rules, preserving explicit equal-prefix precedence. Optional JPA metamodel discovery supplies UUID-valued primary-key and unique-property lookup. JSON configuration uses the shared nested setting vocabulary. Environment variables and Spring properties overlay file values. Configuration loading decides the engine's policy and dependencies before request evaluation begins. Per-engine state and atomic Redis operations Each engine holds a RuntimeStorage.Context . The context combines typed operational stores with RuntimeState for rate counters, form timing, UUID scores, and recent behavior. Creating another engine does not replace the first engine's context. Backend Ownership Behavior across application instances Memory Local engine state. No shared enforcement across instances. File, CSV, SQLite Local persistent store with per-engine request state. Persistence alone does not distribute every request counter. Standalone Redis Shared namespace with versioned keys. Atomic server-side operations coordinate rate, form, UUID, and anomaly state as well as operational stores. The static storage and blacklist helpers remain compatibility facades for CLI and administrative usage; the engine evaluates requests against its own context. Redis failure and upgrade boundaries Java 1.3 supports standalone Redis and validates unsupported Sentinel or Cluster configurations rather than pretending they provide equivalent semantics. Connection, socket, pool-size, and pool-wait limits bound the request's wait for state. fail_closed prevents startup or raises a request-path storage failure when Redis is unavailable. fail_open uses nonblocking enforcement fallbacks and reports failed mutations at the storage boundary. These policies change availability behavior, not model semantics. Versioned keys and a namespace compatibility marker prevent incompatible state schemas from sharing one prefix during an upgrade. A schema mismatch refuses the namespace even under fail_open . Use separate prefixes for separate applications, environments, or intentionally incompatible schemas. Response-derived UUID and anomaly evidence Malformed UUID input contributes an immediate weighted signal. A valid UUID request that returns 404 adds a different probing signal; successful requests can decay the score. The post-response stage supplies the real outcome instead of treating every request as an assumed success. The lazy model provider loads the configured model on demand or through preloading. Scoring builds the Python-aligned six-feature vector, evaluates the forest, and applies threshold and behavior-confirmation rules. Forest availability and sufficient behavior evidence determine whether the AI path can deny a request. Feature What it describes Why it helps path_len Length of the request path. Unusually long probing paths. kw_hits Matches against malicious keywords. Known probing patterns within a path. resp_time Response duration in seconds. Behavior that differs from the normal timing distribution. status_idx An encoded response-status category. Response outcomes without treating status codes as continuous measurements. burst_count Requests associated with the client in the burst window. Rapid repeated activity. total_404 Not-found responses in the relevant per-client history. Repeated discovery of nonexistent routes. The feature order is part of the model contract. A trainer and scorer must agree on the order, status mapping, time units, and window semantics. Summary fields ending in _ms use milliseconds; the feature vector uses seconds. Sharing feature names alone does not make every model artifact interchangeable. New Java models persist safe JSON containing the supported Python Rust-model forest state. Restricted signed legacy Java models remain compatibility inputs, including older feature schemas. A schema match must be checked before exchanging an artifact. Worked example: a missing UUID resource A valid UUID request passes deterministic checks and reaches a Spring controller. The controller returns 404. If the response is uncommitted, the filter supplies that status and duration to the post-response engine. The engine updates weighted UUID behavior, evaluates eligible anomaly evidence, records recent history, and returns the final decision. If the controller already streamed its response, the committed path records the result without replacing it. The observed 404 still matters for subsequent behavior. System overview explains the broader feedback loop; operations covers Redis and model administration. Spring property examples Spring Boot applications are protected automatically. Adding aiwaf-java creates AiwafConfig , AiwafEngine , and the ordered AiwafFilter ; discovers live MVC routes, route annotations, and JPA UUID fields; and applies request controls before the controller plus post-response scoring with the real status and timing. Committed, streaming, and asynchronous responses are recorded but are not replaced after bytes have been sent. Configure the outermost proxy to overwrite client-supplied forwarding headers. Use Redis, a database, or another shared backend when multiple workers must share rate-limit, blacklist, or exemption state. Keep health checks, static assets, and trusted webhook routes explicitly scoped instead of disabling protection globally. Generate a route manifest from the live Spring application rather than supplying controller methods manually: java -cp "your-app.jar:aiwaf-java-1.3.0.jar" \ com.aiwaf.cli.AiwafConsole init \ --app com.example.Application \ --output .aiwaf/paths.json The command starts the application, reads every registered RequestMappingHandlerMapping , writes the shared schema_version/framework/context_hash/routes document, and then closes the temporary application context. At runtime, AiwafEngine loads this file automatically and appends its disabled middleware and rate-limit overrides after explicit pathRules , so explicit equal-prefix rules retain precedence. Set pathManifestEnabled=false or aiwaf.path-manifest.enabled=false to opt out. A valid X-Country value is accepted only from a peer in trustedProxyCidrs ; otherwise AIWAF resolves the client address itself. Default blacklist calls use Python-compatible reputation scoring and temporary escalation (15 minutes, 1 hour, then 24 hours). Use BlacklistManager.blockPermanent(ip, reason) for an explicit permanent administrative block. storageBackend="redis" makes rate-limit buckets, honeypot timing, weighted UUID scores, recent-request anomaly state, blacklist data, exemptions, geo policy, and learned keywords visible to every application instance using the same key prefix. Redis enforcement updates use atomic server-side scripts. Memory, file, CSV, and SQLite engines keep request state isolated per AiwafEngine ; constructing another engine no longer replaces an existing engine's stores. The static RuntimeStorage and BlacklistManager methods remain compatibility facades for command-line and administrative code. The Java 1.3 Redis backend supports standalone Redis only . Sentinel and Cluster configurations are rejected during validation instead of silently operating with incomplete semantics. fail_closed is the default: an unavailable Redis instance prevents startup or raises a request-path storage failure, which results in the application denying availability rather than bypassing protection. fail_open permits startup and returns non-blocking enforcement fallbacks while Redis is unavailable; failed mutations return false at the StorageBackend boundary. Connection, socket, pool size, and pool wait limits are bounded and configurable. RedisStorage.diagnostics() reports operation/failure counts, latency, and live pool utilization. Redis keys include a state-schema version, and each base key prefix has an atomic compatibility marker. Releases using the same schema can share state during a rolling upgrade. A runtime with an incompatible schema refuses the namespace—even in fail_open mode. Use a unique key prefix per application and environment; deploy an incompatible schema with a new prefix, migrate deliberately, then retire the old namespace. Serialized persistent values remain JSON within a schema version. New Java models use the Python-aligned six-feature schema and are written as safe JSON containing the Python aiwaf_rust.IsolationForest state. The main JAR embeds the root license as META-INF/LICENSE . FastR training is optional and falls back to the Java trainer when R or jsonlite is unavailable. Start the application with its existing launcher and request a known non-exempt handler through a browser. Inspect the enabled policy, observed client IP, response status, and duration. Private-address exemptions can affect local tests. Exercise a deliberate block or rate boundary on a staging route, and confirm the handler response is not returned for the rejected request. For distributed deployments, repeat across instances and verify the selected namespace, backend, and failure policy. A successful normal request proves reachability. It does not prove that every middleware is selected or that a trained model is loaded. Use the Java architecture guide to understand request-only versus response-aware decisions. title: Node.js Architecture and Middleware Decisions
text: Node.js Architecture and Middleware Decisions The Node package has one Express-compatible enforcement pipeline. Framework adapters translate their request and response APIs into that pipeline, while storage and model modules provide the state read by each check. On this page Adapter boundary Middleware construction and request planning Actual enforcement sequence What unknown-route anomaly detection means Route analysis becomes a per-request plan State and process boundaries Response hooks and offline learning Optional WASM execution Worked example: one denied request Trace the implementation How AIWAF works: system architecture Adapter boundary js/index.js exports the main middleware and Fastify, Hapi, Koa, NestJS, Next.js API-route, AdonisJS, and Sails adapters. Each adapter maps its framework's request and response methods into the core contract and translates an early rejection back into the framework. Body parsing must happen before protections that inspect parsed fields. Next.js integration uses the Node-style API-handler contract; a Fetch API or Edge request is a different boundary. An adapter is responsible for continuation and response completion, not for maintaining a separate policy implementation. Middleware construction and request planning wafMiddleware.js normalizes configuration, loads path rules, initializes check modules, and creates the middleware function. Each request resolves its path, method, client address, and route plan. shouldApply combines global middleware selection with the route plan. The logger is attached before the ordinary checks when enabled. A shared denial helper records the reason and sends a status with a JSON or text error according to the request and configuration. A rejected request returns early instead of calling the downstream handler. Actual enforcement sequence The current core executes the following sequence for a request. Individual layers run only when enabled and applicable: Attach logging and request timing; resolve the route plan. Enforce the global method policy when enabled. This happens before the request-exemption shortcut. Check IP/path exemptions, then the active blacklist. Validate headers and any enabled WASM header, URL, content, or recent-behavior checks. Apply geo policy, honeypot timing, and rate/flood limits. Inspect static and learned malicious keywords, then UUID probing. Evaluate the eligible unknown-route anomaly path. Attach completed-response keyword learning and call next() for an allowed request. Method rejection can return 405 ; ordinary rate excess can return 429 ; blacklist and other blocking paths can return 403 . The configured checks decide whether a denial also changes IP reputation. What unknown-route anomaly detection means The core compares the requested path with discoverable Express-style routes. If the route table is unavailable or empty, it treats the request as known rather than applying aggressive unknown-route anomaly detection to every proxied request. For an eligible unknown route, the anomaly module scores features. A positive model result alone is insufficient: the model must meet training-volume requirements and recent-behavior analysis must confirm scanning-related activity before the core issues its anomaly block. This gate explains why a suspicious score and an actual denial can differ. Route analysis becomes a per-request plan sourceAst.js uses bounded handler-source analysis to infer API, form, and authentication intent. pathManifest.js combines source signals with live framework route extraction. The compiler turns discovered protections into path overrides; it does not take over the framework router. pathRules.js evaluates those rules with route metadata for each request. Explicit policy can disable one check or override rate limits for a prefix. Rebuilding a manifest is a discovery operation; enforcing its compiled policy is a runtime operation. State and process boundaries Module group State or computation Scope to consider rateLimiter.js Recent timestamps for request-rate windows. An external cache can share the window; the fallback cache is local. Block, exemption, keyword, and geo stores Operational policy and learned data. SQLite and CSV persistence paths differ from distributed request state. anomalyDetector.js and modelStore.js Loaded model and recent behavior. A shared model artifact does not automatically share every behavior buffer. middlewareLogger.js Completed requests and denial reasons. Log persistence supplies evidence and input for offline training. The rate-limiter module initializes its cache from configuration and otherwise uses a process-local fallback. Configure shared state deliberately when multiple Node workers must enforce one limit. Response hooks and offline learning For allowed requests, a response finish hook supplies the actual status to keyword learning. That hook runs after the handler response finishes; it cannot undo an already delivered response. The middleware logger also observes completion. Request logs Completed responses supply paths, client identity, status, and timing. Feature extraction Records are normalized and combined with per-client activity windows. Train and review Volume thresholds gate model training; route exemptions filter learned keywords. Publish artifacts The runtime loads persisted model state and updated learned keywords. The training job is separate from ordinary application request handling. Reading logs and rebuilding a forest does not need to happen for every request. Runtime keyword learning, where enabled, is a separate mechanism that can use completed-response signals. Offline training reads configured access logs or middleware records and persists a language-native forest artifact. Review feature and model compatibility before moving artifacts between Node, Rust/WASM, Python, and Java. Feature What it describes Why it helps path_len Length of the request path. Unusually long probing paths. kw_hits Matches against malicious keywords. Known probing patterns within a path. resp_time Response duration in seconds. Behavior that differs from the normal timing distribution. status_idx An encoded response-status category. Response outcomes without treating status codes as continuous measurements. burst_count Requests associated with the client in the burst window. Rapid repeated activity. total_404 Not-found responses in the relevant per-client history. Repeated discovery of nonexistent routes. The feature order is part of the model contract. A trainer and scorer must agree on the order, status mapping, time units, and window semantics. Summary fields ending in _ms use milliseconds; the feature vector uses seconds. Sharing feature names alone does not make every model artifact interchangeable. Optional WASM execution wasmAdapter.js loads available Rust-backed primitives and converts JavaScript inputs into the WASM representation. The middleware still decides which checks apply, what to log, and when to reject a request. If initialization or conversion is unsuitable, JavaScript implementations remain available. Crossing the binding boundary has a fixed conversion cost. Large feature batches and forest workloads can benefit; small object-heavy calls may be faster in JavaScript. WASM is a computation backend, not a separate HTTP firewall service. Worked example: one denied request A nonexempt request with valid headers reaches the rate limiter. If its shared or local window exceeds the configured maximum, the middleware marks the denial, sends 429 unless a flood or blacklist path determines another status, and returns. The application handler does not run. Logging can still observe the completed denial because its hook was attached earlier. System overview explains the common layers; operations covers CLI, training, and runtime configuration. title: Upgrade and Migration Guide
text: Upgrade and Migration Guide All maintained packages use the AIWAF monorepo . Each package releases independently. Compare the installed version, source manifest, and release notes for your runtime before upgrading; source versions are not confirmation that a registry release exists. Upgrade sequence Record installed versions, enabled middleware, exemptions, configuration, state backend, model path, and proxy behavior. Back up persisted state, configuration, and models. Upgrade one runtime in staging using its package manager or build from a reviewed source revision. Preserve the matching dependency lockfiles. Apply package-name and configuration changes below. Regenerate manifests from the live application after its routes are registered. Migrate blacklist state with the runtime's supported command; inspect counts, expiry, reasons, and exemptions afterward. Regenerate unsupported models with the current trainer. Verify schema, feature order, output location, and load diagnostics. Test normal public traffic, intentional blocks, rate boundaries, intended exemptions, and actual response logging. Test across workers when state is shared. Deploy code, configuration, and compatible state/models together. Reload workers and repeat checks. Keep a compatible rollback snapshot. Node.js package name The npm middleware package is now aiwaf . Replace the old dependency and imports; regenerate the lockfile and test every adapter entrypoint your application uses. npm uninstall aiwaf-js npm install aiwaf const aiwaf = require('aiwaf'); app.use(aiwaf({ AIWAF_MIDDLEWARES: ['all'] })); aiwaf-wasm remains a separate package. Installing it does not replace Node framework middleware. Check normalized aliases and defaults in the configuration reference before moving settings between versions. Python reputation and blacklist data Python 1.0.7 introduced weighted reputation, progressive temporary blocking, expiry, and richer metadata. Legacy blacklist compatibility is backend-aware, including CSV schema detection and conversion of imported permanent blocks. Use the same checkout, environment, and backend configuration as your application: aiwaf blacklist migrate Inspect aiwaf --help and the selected adapter's help when multiple frameworks are installed. Do not manually reinterpret old CSV columns or assume historical permanent blocks retain identical enforcement semantics. Back up first and compare the resulting entries. Python models and Rust acceleration Persisted Python runtime models are JSON. Pickle, joblib, and executable Python-object artifacts are unsupported; use representative logs and the current trainer to create a new model. Check minimum log thresholds rather than forcing production training on a tiny sample. Python 1.0.8 requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.1 for the Rust extra and fixes FastAPI header normalization and the disabled Rust-header path. Supported installed Rust capabilities are selected automatically, with Python fallback. Update the core package and accelerator together, and test header behavior in the real adapter. python -m pip install --upgrade 'aiwaf[flask,rust]' # Use the extra matching your application. aiwaf flask train --help aiwaf flask model --help Route manifests and import targets aiwaf init --framework flask --app app:app aiwaf init --framework flask --app app:create_app aiwaf init --framework fastapi --app app:app aiwaf init --framework django --settings project.settings --app app.py is invalid. The target must be a module and application object/factory. Run discovery in the application's environment; it imports the application. Do not carry a stale manifest across route changes. Java 1.2 and 1.3 changes Java 1.2 adds scoped per-engine storage, distributed Redis enforcement state, Spring Boot live route/annotation discovery, JSON/environment configuration, native MaxMind lookup, and updated reputation behavior. Remove the old requirement for an external mmdblookup executable. Review default private-address exemptions and manifest loading. Java 1.3 adds bounded Redis connection/socket/pool waits, fail-open/fail-closed policy, diagnostics, and state-schema compatibility guards. It supports standalone Redis and rejects Sentinel/Cluster modes. Before a rolling upgrade, test old/new instances with the intended namespace and schema. Do not bypass compatibility guards or point unrelated services at one prefix. Top-level focus: src/ , src/Core/ , src/Adapters/ , src/RateLimit/ , resources/ , tests/ . Design traits: defense-in-depth, exemption-first, conservative AI guardrails, flexible persistence backends. 5. Runtime Entry And Integration Surface Primary API ( src/AIWAF.php ) AIWAF::protect() executes per-request security controls. AIWAF::setPathExistsResolver() enables route-awareness for framework integrations. AIWAF::setMiddlewareDecisionResolver() supports custom middleware gating logic. AIWAF::getLastTrainingTelemetry() exposes latest trainer telemetry snapshot. Typical Bootstrap Load Composer autoload. Initialize selected rate-limit adapter. Call AIWAF::protect() early in front-controller lifecycle. 6. Request Protection Flow ( AIWAF::protect ) Build runtime config via Config::toRuntimeConfig() . Configure rate limiter via configureRateLimiter() (auto-detects db, apcu, redis, or falls back to memory). Resolve request identity ( ip , path ). Exemption short-circuit (skips remaining checks if IP or Path is exempt via configurations or CIDR matches). Method validation (ensures request method is allowed). Header validation (evaluates trust_legitimate_bots , custom_suspicious_patterns , and quality_threshold ). Blocked-IP enforcement. Geo policy checks (compares IP against allow/block countries). AI Anomaly Scoring: Extracts an 8-dimensional feature vector: strlen($path) DynamicKeywordManager::detect($path) 0.5 (baseline structural complexity) Status code anomaly ( 1 if 404/500, else 0 ) Reserved ( 0 ) Reserved ( 0 ) Honeypot trigger ( isset($_POST['aiwaf_honeytrap']) ? 1 : 0 ) UUID tamper check ( UUIDTamperProtector::isSuspicious($path) ? 1 : 0 ) Scores the vector against forest_model.json . If score exceeds threshold, it runs a post-prediction guard ensuring at least one strong signal (e.g., keyword hits ≥ 2.0 or direct honeypot/UUID triggers) before blocking. Rate-limit enforcement (checks max_requests per window_seconds ). Dynamic keyword checks. UUID tamper checks. Honeypot checks (evaluates $_POST payloads). Block responses use 403 for deny cases and 429 for rate-limit violations. AST Static Analysis ( src/Core/ApiDetection.php ) PHP dynamically analyzes controller logic during startup using Abstract Syntax Trees to determine endpoint intent (API vs. Form vs. Auth). This is heavily utilized when native framework routes don't strictly typehint their return models. Parsing: Uses nikic/php-parser ( PhpParser\ParserFactory ) to construct an AST directly from the controller's source file, using reflection ( ReflectionMethod , ReflectionFunction ) to locate the exact start and end lines of the closure or method. Traversal: A custom NodeVisitorAbstract traverses the statements strictly within the bounded line numbers. Call Inspection: Inspects MethodCall , FuncCall , and StaticCall nodes. Increases API confidence if it detects json , json_encode , JsonResponse , or jsonify . Increases Form confidence if it detects view , render , redirect , back , or render_template . Object Instantiation: Inspects New_ nodes. Instantiating JsonResponse yields a high API score. Payload Type: Scans for post , all , input , or file method calls on request objects to flag requestBody = true and classify the expected payload. Path Generation and Auto Middleware ( MiddlewarePlan.php ) AIWAF for PHP includes intelligent path generation and middleware auto-negotiation to dynamically optimize the protection pipeline per endpoint: Route Classification ( PathManifest::classifyRoute ): The manifest generator infers the primary intent of any given route, categorizing paths as api , form , admin , upload , static , or auth . Auto Middleware Planning: Based on the route classification, the engine automatically toggles specific middlewares on or off. For example: API Endpoints: Disables HTML Honeypots, enforces strict JSON payload validation, and allocates a high rate-limit ceiling (120 req/min). Form Endpoints: Enables Honeypot validation, sets strict rate limits (30 req/min), and enforces POST payload sizes. Static Assets: Automatically disables AI Anomaly scoring, Honeypots, and Header Validation to drastically reduce CPU overhead on /static/ or .png routes. Config Sentinels: If requested_middlewares is set to ['auto'] , MiddlewarePlan::planEnabledMiddlewares() dynamically strips out unnecessary middlewares (e.g., completely unloading uuid_tamper if no UUIDs exist, or disabling geo_block if the MMDB isn't configured). Deep Dive: Core Functions and Methods A reference of the core internal functions powering the PHP AIWAF engine. Module / Class Function / Method Description AIWAF.php AIWAF protect() The primary execution gate. Iterates through the resolved middleware plan, terminating the request with a 403 or 429 payload if any middleware rejects. PathManifest.php PathManifest classifyRoute($path, $methods) Matches standard heuristic signatures (e.g., /api/* or /login ) and combines them with AST outputs to bin the route type. ApiDetection.php RouteVisitor enterNode(Node $node) Implements PhpParser\NodeVisitorAbstract to inspect method calls like json() or validate() to build confidence scores for API intents. MiddlewarePlan.php MiddlewarePlan resolve($path, $category) Yields the final array of active middlewares. Trims expensive operations (like HTML honing) when $category === 'api' . detect_and_train.php (CLI Script) extractFeatures($logLine) Parses a line of access logs into the 6-dimension float array needed for training the Isolation Forest. detect_and_train.php (CLI Script) calculateThresholds() Evaluates historical traffic baselines to automatically tune max_req and flood_req dynamically. 7. Drivers in src/RateLimit/ provide backend-specific persistence behavior. 8-9. Storage, Artifacts, Training Lifecycle Artifacts (default under resources/ ) blocked_ips.json , dynamic_keywords.json , request_features.csv , forest_model.json . php setup.php ensures required baseline files exist. Training Pipeline ( AIWAF::detectAndTrain ) The training pipeline executes robust anomaly detection and keyword learning strategies via CLI ( php cli/detect_and_train.php ): Source Processing: Reads from AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG , automatically parsing rotated and gzipped logs via Logs::readRotatedLogs . Feature Extraction: Capable of parallelized feature extraction via FeatureExtractor::pythonFeaturesBatched if Python is available (managed by AIWAF_PYTHON_PARALLEL_WORKERS ). Training Matrix: Extracted per request for the IsolationForest (configured with 200 trees, 32 sample size). The matrix maps 6 dimensions: path_len kw_hits resp_time status_idx burst_count total_404 Anomaly Evaluation: Evaluates the matrix against the model using AIWAF_AI_ANOMALY_THRESHOLD . Identifies anomalous IPs and runs a strict conservative check: keeps burst-only traffic with no suspicious footprint unblocked. Blocks only if: average keyword hits ≥ 2.0, max 404s ≥ 10.0, average burst ≥ 15.0, or total requests ≥ 100. title: AIWAF-PHP Comprehensive Setup Guide
text: Comprehensive Setup AIWAF-PHP Comprehensive Setup Guide How AIWAF works: system architecture Legacy PHP reference. The current monorepo does not contain a PHP package or PHP release workflow. These historical examples have not been validated against the current repo. Use the current Python, Node.js, Java, or Rust/WASM guides for new integrations. 1. What This Guide Is This is an end-to-end setup manual for running aiwaf-php in real PHP applications. Environment prerequisites. Installation for app usage and repository development. Integration patterns for plain PHP, Laravel, Symfony, and WordPress style bootstraps. Baseline and production-oriented configuration. Storage/backend selection for rate limiting. Training workflow and verification. Troubleshooting and validation playbooks. 2. Prerequisites 2.1 Runtime PHP >= 7.4 Composer Optional ext-redis when using Redis adapter/driver 2.2 System dependencies Writable filesystem for resources/ runtime artifacts. Access to application/proxy logs for training ( AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG ). 2.3 Recommended for production Persistent storage for runtime artifacts and model files. Scheduled training runs ( php cli/detect_and_train.php ). Known route/path hints configured to reduce false positives. 3. Installation Paths # Application install composer require aayushgauba/aiwaf # Local development in this repository composer install # Initialize runtime resources php setup.php 4. Core Configuration Concepts AIWAF-PHP can be configured through static config, runtime config, and env mapping in RuntimeConfig::loadFromEnvironment() . Header validation: AIWAF_HEADER_VALIDATION_ENABLED , AIWAF_HEADER_BLOCK_SUSPICIOUS , AIWAF_HEADER_QUALITY_THRESHOLD , AIWAF_HEADER_EXEMPT_PATHS Rate limiting: AIWAF_RATE_LIMITING_ENABLED , AIWAF_RATE_MAX_REQUESTS , AIWAF_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS , AIWAF_EXEMPT_IPS Detection toggles: IP/keyword, honeypot, AI anomaly, UUID tamper toggles Geo policy: allow/block countries Training controls: access log, thresholds, force/disable flags, anomaly threshold, known paths 5. Auto Middleware & Path Manifest Setup AIWAF-PHP can automatically tune your middleware protections based on your application's routing structure. By generating a Path Manifest, AIWAF categorizes your endpoints (e.g., API vs HTML Form) and automatically disables unnecessary middlewares (like Honeypots for APIs) and enforces strict rate limits where appropriate. # Generate the path manifest automatically php cli/detect_and_train.php --generate-manifest At startup, AIWAF reads the manifest from .aiwaf/paths.json to auto-configure the execution chain. If you prefer fine-grained manual control over your middleware stack rather than relying on auto-generation, proceed to the framework-specific "All Middlewares" manual setup sections below. 6. Framework Setup (All Middlewares) WordPress Use integration assets in examples/wordpress/ , including MU-plugin bootstrap and WP-CLI training command. 8. Storage Setup and Backend Choices 7.1 Default behavior Core runtime artifacts are file-backed under resources/ . php setup.php ensures base files exist. 7.2 Key artifact files resources/blocked_ips.json resources/dynamic_keywords.json resources/request_features.csv resources/forest_model.json 7.3 Rate-limit adapter/backend options In-memory adapter APCu adapter Redis adapter DB adapter 9. Training Setup 8.1 Configure training log source # Linux/macOS export AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG=/var/log/nginx/access.log # PowerShell $env:AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG = "C:\path\to\access.log" 8.2 Run training php cli/detect_and_train.php 8.3 Useful training env examples AIWAF_MIN_TRAIN_LOGS=50 AIWAF_MIN_AI_LOGS=10000 AIWAF_FORCE_AI_TRAINING=false AIWAF_DISABLE_AI=false AIWAF_AI_ANOMALY_THRESHOLD=0.65 AIWAF_KNOWN_PATHS=/app,/api,/wp-json 8.4 Expected output Updated keyword store and model artifact when thresholds are met. Trainer telemetry via logs and AIWAF::getLastTrainingTelemetry() . 10. Optional GeoIP Enablement AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_ENABLED=true AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_COUNTRIES=CN,RU # or allowlist mode AIWAF_GEO_ALLOW_COUNTRIES=US,CA Geo checks run in AIWAF::protect() when enabled. 11. Optional Redis/APCu Setup 10.1 Redis adapter example $redis = new Redis(); $redis->connect('127.0.0.1', 6379); RateLimiter::initAdapter(new RedisAdapter($redis)); 10.2 APCu adapter example RateLimiter::initAdapter(new ApcuAdapter()); 12. Production Baseline Checklist [ ] Package installed and app starts with AIWAF enabled. [ ] php setup.php executed in target environment. [ ] Exempt paths set for health/static/known-safe callbacks. [ ] Rate limits tuned from real traffic patterns. [ ] Header policy tuned to reduce false positives. [ ] Training job scheduled and verified. [ ] Intentional block scenario validated in staging. [ ] Runtime artifact paths persisted across deploys/restarts. 13. Validation Playbook Smoke checks: health/static pass, suspicious probe blocks. Rate-limit checks: burst traffic transitions to 429 and/or IP block. Header checks: low-quality headers trigger expected behavior. Training checks: confirm log readability and artifact/telemetry updates. 14. Troubleshooting Training skipped: verify log path/readability and thresholds. Too many false positives: tune exemptions/known paths and anomaly threshold. Not enough detections: lower anomaly threshold carefully and retrain with representative traffic. Redis/APCu issues: verify extension availability/connectivity and fallback to in-memory temporarily. Resource permissions: ensure read/write on resources/ , rerun php setup.php . 15. Contributor Setup (Repository) composer install composer test php setup.php php cli/detect_and_train.php composer run cover-everything composer run test-adapters-matrix composer run validate-all Suggested docs: README.md .

title: Python Framework Adapters
text: Python Framework Adapters How AIWAF works: system architecture Django Add aiwaf.django to INSTALLED_APPS . Use aiwaf.django.middleware.all for the unified stack or explicitly order individual middleware classes. Django supports ORM-backed or CSV runtime stores and file, database, or cache model storage. Apply migrations when using ORM stores. Flask from aiwaf.flask import AIWAF exposes the application integration. Request and response hooks coordinate checks, decorators, logging, and model scoring. Initialize AIWAF once; select middlewares=["auto"] , ["all"] , or a list of canonical middleware names. FastAPI from aiwaf.fast import AIWAF exposes the Starlette-based orchestrator. Pass structured constructor options for storage, header validation, rate limiting, and logging. FastAPI uses the shared runtime storage and route-policy helpers. Version 1.0.8 normalizes headers before Rust validation and respects the adapter's disabled Rust path. Route helpers Django, Flask, and FastAPI expose equivalent route helpers: from aiwaf.flask import ( aiwaf_exempt, aiwaf_exempt_from, aiwaf_only, aiwaf_require_protection, ) @app.get("/health") @aiwaf_exempt def health(): return {"ok": True} @app.post("/webhook") @aiwaf_only("header_validation") def webhook(): return {"accepted": True} Canonical middleware names include header_validation , rate_limit , ip_keyword_block , honeypot , geo_block , uuid_tamper , ai_anomaly , and logging . Middleware selection auto starts from the canonical middleware set and omits checks that are not useful for detected application signals. Route manifests complement live metadata. Generate the manifest from the actual application environment after its routes have been registered. Setup guides Django Flask FastAPI

title: Python Architecture and Request Lifecycle
text: Python Architecture and Request Lifecycle Django, Flask, and FastAPI expose separate adapters over the shared Python core. The adapter owns framework execution; the core supplies route policies, state abstractions, detection helpers, and training primitives. On this page Module boundaries Initialization and policy planning How each adapter executes Following one request Live routes, manifests, and decorators Storage and reputation Training and scoring The Rust acceleration boundary Worked example: an API request and a scanner Trace the implementation How AIWAF works: system architecture Module boundaries Source area Responsibility py/aiwaf/core/ Shared exemptions, middleware planning, route discovery, storage, reputation, training, and native capability bridges. py/aiwaf/django/ Django middleware, ORM models, decorators, settings compatibility, and management commands. py/aiwaf/flask/ Flask application initialization, request/response hooks, stores, and CLI integration. py/aiwaf/fast/ FastAPI-facing exports and middleware; the shared orchestrator lives in core/runtime_fastapi.py . Initialization and policy planning Initialization normalizes settings, selects storage, and resolves the requested middleware set. middleware_plan.py expands canonical selections and applies disabled checks. Route discovery supplies hints such as UUID routes and application intent, while path_manifest.py loads generated path policies. The resulting middleware plan determines which framework hooks are registered. A route plan then decides whether each registered protection applies to a particular request. Global enablement and per-route applicability are different questions. How each adapter executes Adapter Request boundary Response boundary Django The configured MIDDLEWARE order determines nested request execution. The unified alias expands the AIWAF stack; individual classes permit explicit ordering. The framework unwinds response handling through middleware. Logging and checks that use outcomes need to observe that response. Flask flask_integration.py registers selected middleware objects and their Flask request hooks. A returned response stops normal handler dispatch. Response hooks observe the handler result for logging and relevant behavior checks. FastAPI runtime_fastapi.py registers Starlette middleware in reverse order because the last registered wrapper executes first. Response control returns through the wrapper chain; the orchestrator coordinates configuration and lifecycle integration. FastAPI's orchestrator documents the effective available chain as Geo, IP/keyword, Rate, AI, Honeypot, UUID, Header, and Logging. Disabled or inapplicable layers are skipped. Do not infer execution order from the order of add_middleware calls alone. Following one request Resolve context Read request metadata and the resolved endpoint where available. Apply route policy Check path rules and endpoint exemption or protection metadata for each layer. Enforce selected checks Consult block state, counters, validation rules, and the available anomaly model. Observe outcome Allow the handler or return a denial, then record the response through applicable hooks. The exact shortcut behavior belongs to each middleware. An exempt path, an exempt client, a geo-only exemption, and a decorator disabling one check are distinct policies. Use the layer-specific decision to explain a bypass rather than assuming that every exemption disables the complete stack. Live routes, manifests, and decorators The CLI imports the actual application object or Django URL configuration and enumerates registered routes. Where handler source is available, static analysis adds method, API, form, and authentication signals. The generated .aiwaf/paths.json is a policy input, not a replacement router. Manifest compilation creates path rules for middleware enablement and rate overrides. Explicit decorators carry endpoint intent: aiwaf_exempt , aiwaf_exempt_from , aiwaf_only , and aiwaf_require_protection . They complement global configuration. Regenerate a manifest when live registrations change so the policy does not describe an older application. Storage and reputation The shared runtime storage layer provides memory, JSON-file, CSV, and SQLite key-value implementations and typed stores for blocks, exemptions, keywords, and geo policy. Django and Flask also provide framework-specific database and CSV paths. A storage choice is adapter-specific; model storage is configured separately. Reputation-based blacklisting stores weighted offenses, temporary-block escalation, expiration, and metadata. A later request reads that state rather than recomputing an entire traffic history. Legacy blacklist migration converts older schemas into the richer representation. Memory is local to a process. Persisting an operational store does not automatically make every rate bucket or recent-request buffer distributed. FastAPI can supply a Redis-backed rate cache; review the storage semantics of the other enabled checks separately. Training and scoring Feature What it describes Why it helps path_len Length of the request path. Unusually long probing paths. kw_hits Matches against malicious keywords. Known probing patterns within a path. resp_time Response duration in seconds. Behavior that differs from the normal timing distribution. status_idx An encoded response-status category. Response outcomes without treating status codes as continuous measurements. burst_count Requests associated with the client in the burst window. Rapid repeated activity. total_404 Not-found responses in the relevant per-client history. Repeated discovery of nonexistent routes. The feature order is part of the model contract. A trainer and scorer must agree on the order, status mapping, time units, and window semantics. Summary fields ending in _ms use milliseconds; the feature vector uses seconds. Sharing feature names alone does not make every model artifact interchangeable. Request logs Completed responses supply paths, client identity, status, and timing. Feature extraction Records are normalized and combined with per-client activity windows. Train and review Volume thresholds gate model training; route exemptions filter learned keywords. Publish artifacts The runtime loads persisted model state and updated learned keywords. The training job is separate from ordinary application request handling. Reading logs and rebuilding a forest does not need to happen for every request. Runtime keyword learning, where enabled, is a separate mechanism that can use completed-response signals. The trainer parses logs, extracts behavior, filters legitimate route tokens from keyword learning, and trains only when configured volume thresholds permit. Request-time scoring reads an available model; lack of a usable model does not remove deterministic header, rate, keyword, or geo controls. Model artifacts carry forest state and metadata in JSON. Current Python persistence does not load pickle or joblib objects. That serialization boundary is separate from the choice of file, database, or cache for storing the artifact. The Rust acceleration boundary rust_backend.py discovers installed aiwaf_rust capabilities. A supported native operation can accelerate matching, header validation, feature extraction, or forest operations while the Python adapter continues to own the request and response. The bridge normalizes HTTP and WSGI header names before calling native validation. If the extension or a capability is unavailable, the relevant Python fallback remains available. Native acceleration changes where a computation runs; it does not replace framework policy or storage. Worked example: an API request and a scanner A JSON API handler can carry route metadata that omits HTML form timing. Header and rate checks still apply when selected. Allowed requests reach the handler, and the logger records its actual result. A scanner requesting many missing paths creates a different record: suspicious keyword hits, repeated 404s, and burst activity. Keyword or rate checks may reject it immediately. Sufficient logs later give the trainer behavior data for the anomaly path. Each decision should be explainable by its enabled layer and recorded reason. System overview connects these components. The setup guides show wiring, and operations covers migration and training commands. Trace the implementation Follow these files in the monorepo to connect the architecture to the code: py/aiwaf/core/middleware_plan.py py/aiwaf/core/path_manifest.py py/aiwaf/core/runtime_fastapi.py py/aiwaf/flask/flask_integration.py py/aiwaf/django/middleware.py py/aiwaf/core/runtime_blacklist.py py/aiwaf/core/rust_backend.py

title: Python Operations and Migration
text: Python Operations and Migration How AIWAF works: system architecture Unified CLI # Unified CLI aiwaf --help aiwaf blacklist migrate aiwaf status # Django management commands python manage.py detect_and_train python manage.py regenerate_model python manage.py aiwaf_reset --keywords --confirm python manage.py aiwaf_logging --status python manage.py geo_block_country list # Explicit adapter dispatch aiwaf django aiwaf_list --all aiwaf flask --help aiwaf fast --help The CLI detects the framework from an explicit selection, application object, or installed framework. If several frameworks are installed, pass --framework or --app . Run aiwaf --help for the current dispatch options. Blacklist migration Version 1.0.7 introduced weighted reputation, progressively longer temporary blocks, expiration, and richer blacklist metadata. Existing blacklist data has compatibility handling; aiwaf blacklist migrate performs backend-aware migration. Legacy CSV schemas are detected and imported permanent blocks are converted safely. Review existing entries and back up runtime state before migration. Model storage Persisted Python models use JSON state. Pickle, joblib, and executable Python-object formats are unsupported. Regenerate old model artifacts through the current trainer. Installing aiwaf-rust enables available acceleration automatically, with Python fallback for missing capabilities. Local development and verification Run from the monorepo root: python -m pip install -e ".[django,flask,fastapi,rust]" python -m pip install pytest pytest-cov coverage httpx npm ci --prefix js python aiwaf_test.py --python-only pytest python -m benchmarks.benchmark_auto_middleware Independent releases The next ELv2 release candidates below have not been published. Release versions and tags must match the relevant manifest. Package Manifest Tag Workflow Python aiwaf pyproject.toml python-v1.1.2 python-publish.yml npm aiwaf js/package.json js-v1.1.2 npm-publish.yml PyPI aiwaf-rust rust/pyproject.toml + rust/Cargo.toml rust-v0.2.2 rust-publish.yml npm aiwaf-wasm rust/crates/aiwaf_wasm/Cargo.toml wasm-v0.2.2 wasm-publish.yml Maven aiwaf-java java/pom.xml java-v1.3.3 java-publish.yml Python and Rust publish to PyPI with trusted publishing. The npm workflows use npm trusted publishing and stage packages for approval. Configure the trusted publisher with organization aiwaf-project , repository aiwaf , the exact workflow filename, and the environment used by that workflow. Java publishing uses the protected maven-publish environment plus GPG_PRIVATE_KEY , GPG_PASSPHRASE , CENTRAL_TOKEN_USERNAME , and CENTRAL_TOKEN_PASSWORD . The workflow verifies the tag, runs tests, signs the POM and all three JARs, uploads the deployment bundle, and waits for Maven Central publication. Registry releases are immutable. Increment the relevant manifest version before publishing another release. Deployment Configure the application to trust forwarding headers only from known proxy CIDRs. Configure the outermost proxy to overwrite client-supplied forwarding headers. Use Redis, a database, or another shared backend when multiple workers must share rate-limit, blacklist, or exemption state. Keep health checks, static assets, and trusted webhook routes explicitly scoped instead of disabling protection globally. Start anomaly detection in observe-only or conservative mode and tune it with representative normal traffic. Rotate logs and exclude secrets, authorization headers, cookies, and personal data. Sign model/configuration artifacts where the runtime supports HMAC verification. Run AIWAF alongside normal secure-development controls and an edge/reverse-proxy layer.

title: Django Setup
text: Django Setup How AIWAF works: system architecture Add AIWAF to a Django application and verify that protection is registered with the live route table. Before you begin Use an environment compatible with your framework. This guide assumes an existing Django project with manage.py and a settings module. New to middleware? Start with the six-step first protected app tutorial , which includes complete files and expected responses. 1. Install the framework extra pip install "aiwaf[django]" pip install "aiwaf[rust]" # optional native acceleration Install into the environment used to run your application. Choose an interpreter compatible with the framework and dependencies. 2. Register protection project/settings.py (merge into existing lists) Add the app and the unified middleware alias in settings.py : INSTALLED_APPS = [ # ... "aiwaf.django", ] MIDDLEWARE = [ "django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware", "aiwaf.django.middleware.all", # ... ] For explicit ordering, replace the alias with the individual middleware classes: MIDDLEWARE = [ "aiwaf.django.middleware.JsonExceptionMiddleware", "aiwaf.django.middleware.GeoBlockMiddleware", "aiwaf.django.middleware.IPAndKeywordBlockMiddleware", "aiwaf.django.middleware.RateLimitMiddleware", "aiwaf.django.middleware.AIAnomalyMiddleware", "aiwaf.django.middleware.HoneypotTimingMiddleware", "aiwaf.django.middleware.UUIDTamperMiddleware", "aiwaf.django.middleware.HeaderValidationMiddleware", "aiwaf.django.middleware_logger.AIWAFLoggerMiddleware", ] Protection middleware should run early. Logging should run late enough to observe the application response. 3. Discover your live routes Run from the application checkout after all routes are registered: aiwaf init --framework django --settings project.settings The default output is .aiwaf/paths.json . Flask and FastAPI require module:object in --app ; Flask factories such as app:create_app are supported. Repeat discovery when registered routes change. 4. Scope route exemptions project/views.py from django.http import JsonResponse from aiwaf.django import aiwaf_exempt, aiwaf_only @aiwaf_exempt def health(request): return JsonResponse({"ok": True}) @aiwaf_only("header_validation") def webhook(request): return JsonResponse({"accepted": True}) Merge these paths into your existing Django URL configuration, keeping other project routes: project/urls.py from django.urls import path from .views import health, webhook urlpatterns = [ path("health/", health), path("webhook/", webhook), # Keep your existing paths here. ] Apply migrations for ORM-backed stores: python manage.py makemigrations aiwaf python manage.py migrate python manage.py check 5. Configure settings and model storage Define flat AIWAF_* settings in your Django settings module. Merge the app and middleware into existing lists rather than replacing your authentication/session middleware. Area Important settings Training AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG , AIWAF_MIN_TRAIN_LOGS , AIWAF_MIN_AI_LOGS , AIWAF_FORCE_AI_TRAINING Rate limiting AIWAF_RATE_WINDOW , AIWAF_RATE_MAX , AIWAF_RATE_FLOOD Headers AIWAF_REQUIRED_HEADERS , AIWAF_HEADER_QUALITY_MIN_SCORE Honeypot AIWAF_MIN_FORM_TIME , AIWAF_MAX_PAGE_TIME UUID checks AIWAF_UUID_SCORE_ENABLED , AIWAF_UUID_SCORE_BLOCK_THRESHOLD GeoIP AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_ENABLED , AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_COUNTRIES , AIWAF_GEO_ALLOW_COUNTRIES Exemptions AIWAF_EXEMPT_PATHS , AIWAF_EXEMPT_KEYWORDS , AIWAF_ALLOWED_PATH_KEYWORDS Models AIWAF_MODEL_PATH , AIWAF_MODEL_STORAGE , AIWAF_MODEL_STORAGE_FALLBACK When aiwaf_rust is importable, supported acceleration paths are selected automatically. Python remains the fallback when a native capability is unavailable. Persisted runtime models use JSON state; AIWAF does not load pickle, joblib, or other executable Python-object formats. 6. Check and run Django python manage.py check python manage.py migrate python manage.py runserver The settings snippet does not create an application view. Request http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/ after registering the health view as shown above. It should return {"ok": true} . Then test a non-exempt application route for normal and rejected traffic; health is deliberately exempt. python manage.py detect_and_train --help python manage.py regenerate_model --help Use Python operations for training, model inspection, and state migration. Training requires representative logs in a supported format; setup alone does not train a model. Production configuration Configure the application to trust forwarding headers only from known proxy CIDRs. Configure the outermost proxy to overwrite client-supplied forwarding headers. Use Redis, a database, or another shared backend when multiple workers must share rate-limit, blacklist, or exemption state. Keep health checks, static assets, and trusted webhook routes explicitly scoped instead of disabling protection globally. Start anomaly detection in observe-only or conservative mode and tune it with representative normal traffic. Rotate logs and exclude secrets, authorization headers, cookies, and personal data. Sign model/configuration artifacts where the runtime supports HMAC verification. Run AIWAF alongside normal secure-development controls and an edge/reverse-proxy layer.
